title: Partial Success Management
summary: Represent completed, failed, and unknown sub-results explicitly so a workflow can deliver useful work without misrepresenting completion.
overview: Partial success management defines what an aggregate task means when only some branches complete. A portfolio report may remain useful with one unavailable data source, while a settlement calculation may require every mandatory input. The acceptance rule must be a business contract rather than an accidental consequence of whichever promises resolved first.

Each branch needs a stable identity, status, provenance, and freshness. Distinguish failed, timed out, skipped, and unknown outcomes; an empty result is not equivalent to a successful search with zero matches. Aggregation then uses mandatory dependencies, optional enrichment, quorum rules where appropriate, or explicit incomplete delivery.

production.poc: In a prototype, force one branch to fail and inspect whether the answer falsely claims complete coverage.
production.production: Production defines branch contracts, independent retries, durable progress, and a response schema that exposes missing information.
production.scale: Enterprise workflows need incremental updates, ownership of unresolved branches, bounded retention, and reporting that separates task completion from branch completion.

components.name: Task manifest
components.role: Lists requested branches, required inputs, and completion rules.

components.name: Branch executors
components.role: Run independent work and return typed status with evidence.

components.name: Progress store
components.role: Persists individual outcomes and supports selective retry.

components.name: Aggregation policy
components.role: Decides whether available evidence supports a complete, partial, or blocked result.

components.name: Result presentation
components.role: Shows coverage, missing sections, freshness, and any pending follow-up.

flow.title: Create manifest
flow.description: Assign branch identifiers and classify mandatory versus optional inputs before execution.

flow.title: Execute independently
flow.description: Run branches within their own deadlines and resource limits.

flow.title: Persist outcomes
flow.description: Record success, error, timeout, or unknown with source and attempt information.

flow.title: Evaluate coverage
flow.description: Apply the task acceptance rule to the available results rather than counting successful calls alone.

flow.title: Publish qualified result
flow.description: Expose missing coverage and prevent unsupported conclusions from entering the narrative.

flow.title: Repair selectively
flow.description: Retry only eligible failed branches and publish a new result revision when evidence changes.

useCase.title: Preparing a morning exposure briefing
useCase.situation: A research agent gathers positions, ledger balances, regional market data, and explanatory commentary.
useCase.problem: A commentary provider is unavailable while core position data is complete.
useCase.requirement: Publish a useful briefing with an accurate statement of coverage and no invented missing analysis.
useCase.architecture: A task manifest marks positions and balances mandatory and commentary optional.
runtime: Branch results are stored independently with timestamps.
The aggregator publishes exposures and labels commentary unavailable, then schedules a targeted retry.
useCase.failure: If position data fails instead, the report remains blocked because the central exposure claim cannot be supported.
useCase.impact: Monitor incomplete-report rate, time to repair missing branches, and operator comprehension of coverage; partial delivery must remain visibly partial.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires users to understand incomplete coverage.

tradeoffs.benefit: Allow selective repair without rerunning everything.
tradeoffs.cost: Require revision-aware consumers and notification rules.

failures.detection: Aggregate totals look complete despite unavailable data.
failures.recovery: Use explicit unknown states and block unsupported calculations.

failures.detection: A stale branch result arrives after a fresh revision.
failures.recovery: Compare source versions and reject obsolete updates.

mistakes.mistake: Returning HTTP success as proof of complete work
mistakes.fix: Include a structured task-level completion status.
Retry failed branches by identity and retain valid outcomes.
Expose coverage in the response contract and user interface.

whenToUse: Use for independent research or enrichment branches.
Use when optional data can arrive after the primary result.
Use for batch tasks with item-level outcomes.
whenNotToUse: Avoid partial completion for indivisible transactional invariants.
Do not combine incomparable source timestamps silently.
Avoid presenting incomplete evidence as a final recommendation.
checklist: Prevent unknown values from becoming zeros.
Version aggregate results when late evidence arrives.
